You are working in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; run `.venv/bin/python` (never uv). Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code. Tests may use the shipped continuity-initiative package through the helpers in tests/test_observation_mode.py (`_state_at`) and tests/test_observation_shadow.py, plus a synthetic second story. Write the tests FIRST, run them and confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. Do not edit any file outside YOU MAY EDIT ONLY. Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. BACKGROUND. RuntimeEngine._turn_active (storygame/runtime/engine.py) loops up to TURN_NARRATION_ATTEMPTS=2 times: provider call, reveal resolve, validate_effects, a deepcopy `candidate_state` with `apply_proposal(proposal, apply_world=False)`, then narration_validator.validate; a ProposalValidationError on the first attempt triggers one retry with provider.note_rejection(code). Only AFTER the loop does it call state.apply_proposal(proposal) and then WorldCapture.after_commit(command, narration, entered_scene=...), which calls ItemFactsProvider.apply_item_facts(raw, ...) and that MUTATES state.facts (World over state.facts), provider fields and makes billed model calls: one item-facts match call via CloudflareTurnProvider._request_item_facts and Jev mapping checks through the `confirm` lambda. Observation context: ItemFactsProvider._observation_context() and storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py (ObservationVerifier, relations_from_context, fail-closed verdicts; `report.accepted` is True only when outcome is 'ok' and every verdict is 'accept'). The verifier is already built and must not change. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/engine.py and tests/test_observation_enforcement.py (NEW). 

CONTEXT. T8a/T8a2 are done and tested: read storygame/runtime/observation_preview.py and WorldCapture.preview_commit / take_preview / after_commit / before_turn / context / resume / discard in storygame/runtime/capture.py, and tests/test_observation_preview.py. `WorldCapture.enforcing_verifier` is None in the product, so enforcement is OFF unless a test sets it; the engine must be byte-identical in behavior when it is None (the existing suites are the proof). `capture.after_commit` records `observation_preview` and `observation_diverged` when it consumed a required preview. 

GOAL (T8b): wire the preview into RuntimeEngine._turn_active as ONE shared recovery path, with exact rollback. Do not add a third narration call: the loop keeps TURN_NARRATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 and the per-turn narration budget. 

BUILD. (1) Inside the existing attempt loop, in the same `try` as `self.narration_validator.validate(...)`, directly after it, call a new private method `_preview_observation(command_text, proposal, candidate_state, before)` that does nothing when `self.capture is None`; otherwise calls `self.capture.preview_commit(command_text, proposal.narration, candidate_state, entered_scene=candidate_state.current_scene_id != before.current_scene_id)` and, when the returned preview is not accepted, raises `ProposalValidationError('The narration did not show the observed things as the world has them.', code='observation_unverified')` (generic message: no thing names, no narration, no model text). That exception flows into the EXISTING `except ProposalValidationError` retry branch (same bookkeeping: guard_rejections, `provider.note_rejection(code)` with NO term, `guard_retry_used`, budget check, last attempt re-raises) so nothing is duplicated. Remember the accepted preview's narration in a local variable `previewed_narration` (None when no required preview). (2) Before `self.capture.before_turn(...)`, when `self.capture` is set, take `pre_turn_context = self.capture.context()`. In the `except (ProposalValidationError, RuntimeContractError)` block, after the existing `self.capture.discard()` and snapshot restore, when the error code is 'observation_unverified' or 'observation_diverged' also call `self.capture.resume(pre_turn_context)` so no provider field from the rejected turn survives (held item facts, changed names, unplaced lists, prior steps). The same restoration is done on the divergence path below. (3) At commit: when `previewed_narration` is not None pass `previewed_narration` (not the possibly hand-off-extended proposal.narration) as the `narration` argument of `self.capture.after_commit`, so the preview is consumed and its billed answers replayed. Directly after after_commit, if `capture_record.get('observation_diverged')` is true: `self.capture.discard()`, `self.state.restore_snapshot(before)`, `self.capture.resume(pre_turn_context)`, `self._clear_provider_handoff()`, record the attempt with outcome 'rejected' and `AttemptError(code='observation_diverged', message='The committed effects differ from the previewed effects.')`, and raise `ProposalValidationError(message, code='observation_diverged')`. No success text, segments or facts may remain. (4) Leave the game-break paths, `_handle_refusal`, pacing and `_complete_accepted_turn` unchanged; the preview must never be taken twice for one attempt, and a preview left over from a rejected attempt must not be consumed by the next attempt (before the second attempt's preview, take_preview semantics already drop mismatches; add a test). 

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_observation_enforcement.py (hermetic; find a working engine+capture fixture in tests/test_narration_retry.py, tests/test_3c_world_capture_wiring.py, tests/test_boarding.py, tests/test_observation_mode.py and tests/test_observation_preview.py; a scripted narration provider that returns proposals with different narrations and item_facts per attempt is expected; fake `ask` returning noul scores; count every provider/narration call, match call and confirm call). Required: 1 enforcement off (default): preview_commit is never called (spy), behavior unchanged. 2 accepted on attempt 1: exactly 1 narration call, world committed equals a run with no enforcing verifier, exactly one match call and one set of confirm calls in total (replay), record has observation_preview accepted and observation_diverged False. 3 rejected then accepted: 2 narration calls, provider.note_rejection received code 'observation_unverified' with no term, guard_retry_used True, the first attempt's item facts are in NO committed fact (assert on facts and on the final record), match calls at most 2 for the whole turn. 4 rejected twice: the turn raises ProposalValidationError with code 'observation_unverified'; narration calls == 2 (never 3); `state.snapshot()` equals the pre-turn snapshot on every field including turn_index and last_turn_delivery; the generic vars(provider) snapshot (same helper idea as tests/test_observation_preview.py, excluding billing counters) equals the pre-turn one; the attempt is recorded 'rejected' with that code; no segments committed. 5 verifier unavailable (ask returns None) and uncertain scores behave as rejection (fail closed), not as acceptance. 6 verifier requests: at most 1 per attempt and 2 per turn; a new turn resets them. 7 divergence at commit: make the real application differ from the preview (for example wrap state.apply_proposal to also move an item, or alter facts the application reads) -> ProposalValidationError code 'observation_diverged', snapshot and provider fields exactly restored, nothing committed. 8 a boarding turn (observation kind 'enter') that is rejected once then accepted seats the protagonist exactly once, increments turn_index once, fires each pacing event once, and consumes prior_steps once (no double seating, no repeated pacing). 9 forced-handoff turn or a complication_verbatim turn (find a fixture; if none exists build the smallest one) with enforcement: the preview is consumed (no live match call at commit), the committed turn succeeds. If you cannot build either, say so and assert via a spy that after_commit receives the previewed narration. 10 a NarrationProviderError raised inside the preview (item-facts budget exhausted) surfaces as the existing operational failure: state and provider fields restored, attempt recorded 'operational_failure'. 11 a turn with no observation request but an enforcing verifier set: no verifier request, no behavior change. 12 a synthetic second-story engine run (tiny package as in tests/test_observation_context.py) shows accept, reject-once and reject-twice behaviors. 

FINISH: run the engine-related suites listed in the check, ruff check and format; report counts and quote the new engine code.
